newsitem.title: UK: Copper charges to 1-year high in speculative rally.
newsitem.headline: Copper charges to 1-year high in speculative rally.

text.p: Copper prices flew to the strongest levels in nearly a year on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Thursday as speculators piled in and amid heightened fears of shortages.
Three month LME prices knocked down several barriers, matching prices not seen since huge trading losses by Sumitomo Corp last June rocked the market.
They touched $2,475 per tonne, up $61 on the day and the highest since May 30, 1996 before wilting slightly on profit-taking.
Last business on the afternoon kerb was at $2,463.
The buying was widespread, including short-covering, investment fund interest and technical moves as prices surmounted the key $2,440 area.
The premium of cash over three month metal zoomed to over $100, nearly doubling since Wednesday. It was as high as $110 at one point, but dipped along with futures to end the afternoon at $90/$95.
The market is becoming jittery as stocks resume falling amid good offtake by consumers and continued supply difficulties.
LME stocks dropped by 3,225 tonnes on Thursday to 146,075 tonnes.
"I still think we have further to go. There is danger of more tightness," said analyst Willliam Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff.

A maintenance closedown of a Kennecott smelter in the U.S., although planned, was helping to keep the market tight, Adams said. It was due to reopen next month and may take some steam out of the market.

In Chile, the world's largest producer, smelters have had difficulties due to water supply problems and workers at the huge Chuquicamata mine are in talks on a wage contract which expires at the end of the month.
Technically, the next main target is $2,500, but the market is entering a sticky area of resistance between $2,450 and $2,600, Adams said.
All the other metals ended with gains, but none were as strong as copper's.
Aluminium hit $1,675, but heavy forward producer selling came in to take advantage of the high prices, traders said.
It ended the kerb only $2 firmer at $1,658.
The market has been targeting its year high around $1,700, but has struggled despite hefty stock falls, like Thursday's of 3,750 tonnes.
Zinc also explored higher levels, touching $1,358, but ended only $5 stronger at $1,344.
Lead and tin kept within recent ranges, adding $4 to $626 and $35 to $5,770 respectively.
Alloy was indicated little changed at $1,510/20.
